Q1.answer: Forecasters normalized with training statistics mis-scale inputs when the series' level shifts after training/deployment, raising error. The paper asks whether rolling-window (per-window) normalization removes that error without hurting unshifted accuracy.

Q2.answer: The paper asserts level shifts are the most common failure mode of deployed forecasters and that training-statistics normalization is near-universal, so the mis-scaling would be widespread. Both assertions rest on citations whose reference list is omitted.
Q2.missing: Verifiable support for the prevalence claims; reference list is omitted.

Q3.answer: In the evaluations the authors examined, normalization and model size were changed together, so the effect of normalization alone was confounded with capacity.
Q3.missing: The gap is stated in one sentence with one citation; it is also in tension with the claim that prior work already showed per-window normalization fixes distribution shift in general.

Q4.answer: Generated a synthetic hourly series (SynthLoad) following [R4], injected level shifts of 0.2-0.8 training SDs, and compared a training-statistics baseline, RWN (statistics of last 48 steps) and RWN-fixed (statistics frozen after first 48 post-shift steps), all using the same MLP, 5 seeds, measuring MAE.
Q4.missing: Which statistics (mean/SD?), input window and horizon lengths, how outputs are de-normalized, when the shift occurs, test-set size, and SynthLoad generation details.

Q5.answer: Holding the model fixed isolates normalization from capacity (the confound in prior evaluations); RWN-fixed isolates the contribution of continued adaptation. No rationale is given for the 48-step window, the MLP, or the synthetic data.
Q5.missing: Justification for window length, architecture and synthetic benchmark.

Q6.answer: MAE comparison of baseline vs RWN at no shift and at shifts s in {0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8}, plus an ablation with RWN-fixed, 5 seeds each, on one synthetic series.

Q7.answer: Unshifted MAE indistinguishable (RWN 0.409 +/- 0.007 vs baseline 0.412 +/- 0.006); RWN reduced MAE 11-29% for s = 0.2-0.6; freezing statistics retains about two thirds of the gain.
Q7.missing: Per-shift MAE values and seed variability under shift; the ablation numbers.

Q8.answer: On this one synthetic series with a fixed MLP, RWN costs nothing without shift and reduces error for moderate level shifts, and most of that gain comes from re-estimating statistics once after the shift rather than continuously.

Q9.answer: Not established: any benefit at s = 0.8; behavior on real data, other shift types, other architectures/capacities or tuned windows; that capacity plays no role (capacity was never varied); general claims about distribution shift.

Q10.answer: A capacity-controlled comparison showing per-window normalization helps under moderate level shift without harming unshifted accuracy, with a boundary at the largest shift and an ablation attributing about a third of the gain to continued adaptation.

Q11.answer: Synthetic data only, fixed capacity, untuned window, level shifts only; also (not stated by authors) a single series, 5 seeds, no reported variability under shift, and omitted references.

Q12.answer: Rolling-window normalization cut MAE by 11-29% for moderate level shifts on a synthetic series at no unshifted cost, but not at the largest shift, and most of the gain comes from a single re-estimation of statistics.

location.quote: a level shift after deployment mis-scales every input

findings.observed: The problem (training-statistics normalization mis-scales inputs after a level shift) is stated concretely in the first sentence.
findings.reader_struggle: Works: readers immediately know the failure mechanism being addressed.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers correctly identify the problem.
findings.revision_principle: Keep the mechanism-first problem statement.

location.quote: Level shifts are the most common failure mode of deployed forecasters [R1]

findings.observed: Motivation rests on sweeping prevalence claims ('most common', 'essentially all') backed only by citations whose reference list is omitted.
findings.reader_struggle: An expert doubts the superlatives and cannot check them; a verifier has nothing to verify.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers discount the motivation or accept unverified superlatives.
findings.revision_principle: Motivate with claims scoped to what cited evidence shows, and make the evidence checkable.

location.quote: RQ1: does per-window normalization reduce error under level shift without harming unshifted accuracy?

findings.observed: Two explicit, answerable research questions.
findings.reader_struggle: Minor friction: RQ2 'how much of the gain' does not specify at which shift magnitude.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers know what is asked; the RQ2 answer's scope is ambiguous.
findings.revision_principle: State the conditions under which each question is answered.

location.quote: Our contributions are a capacity-controlled comparison, a boundary at the largest shift

findings.observed: Contributions are listed, but 'capacity-controlled' only means capacity was held fixed, not varied; and the novelty is undercut by the claim that prior work already showed per-window normalization fixes distribution shift in general.
findings.reader_struggle: An expert asks what is new if [R2] already settled the question.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers are unsure whether the contribution is a new finding or a replication.
findings.revision_principle: Position the contribution against prior work accurately, without claims that make the study appear redundant.

location.quote: RWN uses the statistics of the most recent 48 steps

findings.observed: Which statistics, how inputs/outputs are (de)normalized, input window and horizon, when the shift occurs relative to the test period, and the MLP configuration are unspecified; SynthLoad is defined only by reference to [R4].
findings.reader_struggle: Audience is not assumed to know forecasting normalization practice or the benchmark, so readers must guess the mechanism.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers cannot reproduce or fully understand how RWN differs operationally from the baseline.
findings.revision_principle: Define every procedure the audience is not assumed to know, in enough detail to reproduce it.

location.quote: All use the same multilayer perceptron with 5 seeds.

findings.observed: One synthetic series, one architecture, one window size, 5 seeds; no test-set size, no statistical test; RWN-fixed freezes statistics at a known post-shift time (oracle knowledge of shift onset).
findings.reader_struggle: A verifier cannot judge whether the design supports the claims or whether RWN-fixed is a realistic comparator.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers treat the ablation result as less informative than presented.
findings.revision_principle: Describe the experimental design fully, including what information each variant has access to.

location.quote: Under shift, RWN reduced MAE by 11–29% across s = 0.2–0.6 (Figure 1)

findings.observed: Unshifted result is reported with mean and SD, but shifted results are only a percentage range with no per-shift values or seed variability; the s = 0.8 and ablation results have no numbers at all.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers cannot tell which shift gives 11% vs 29% or whether gains exceed seed noise.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers accept a range they cannot inspect.
findings.revision_principle: Report every headline result with values and variability at each condition.

location.quote: stale statistics, rather than capacity, account for much of the error here

findings.observed: Interpretation is hedged ('suggest', 'here'), but contrasts statistics with capacity although capacity was never varied.
findings.reader_struggle: An expert notes that holding capacity fixed cannot show capacity's relative contribution.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers may take away a comparative claim the design cannot support.
findings.revision_principle: Interpret only along factors that were actually manipulated.

location.quote: Limitations: synthetic data, fixed capacity, untuned window, level shifts only.

findings.observed: Limitations are disclosed but as a terse list; they are not used to bound the introduction's general claims, and single-series/5-seed/oracle-freeze issues are not mentioned.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers must work out themselves what each limitation implies for the claims.
findings.likely_consequence: The scope of the findings is underappreciated.
findings.revision_principle: State what each limitation means for which claim, and apply it consistently throughout.

location.quote: Prior work has shown that per-window normalization fixes distribution shift in general [R2].

findings.observed: The story (problem -> confound -> controlled test -> boundary -> ablation) is coherent, but the claim that prior work already solved the general case contradicts the need for the study.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers are confused why a settled question is re-asked.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers question the paper's premise.
findings.revision_principle: Ensure framing of prior work is consistent with the gap the paper fills.

location.quote: added level shifts of s in {0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8} training standard deviations

findings.observed: MAE and shift units are defined, but 'normalization with training statistics', 'per-window normalization' and 'statistics' are never operationally defined; 'per-window' and 'rolling-window' are used interchangeably.
findings.reader_struggle: The audience is explicitly not assumed to know forecasting normalization practice.
findings.likely_consequence: Non-specialist robustness researchers guess the mechanism.
findings.revision_principle: Define domain-specific terms at first use and use one name per concept.

location.quote: In the evaluations we examined, normalization and model size were changed together [R3].

findings.observed: The step from prior work to the gap is abrupt, and it follows a sentence claiming the question was already answered; results and discussion otherwise follow the RQs in order.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers must reconcile 'already shown' with 'confounded'.
findings.likely_consequence: The gap appears weaker than intended.
findings.revision_principle: Make each step of the argument follow from the previous one without contradiction.

location.quote: [R1]–[R6] Reference list omitted in this manuscript version.

findings.observed: All six citations are untraceable; the benchmark protocol is delegated to [R4]; results are said to be consistent with [R5] and [R6] without detail; Figure 1 is not present.
findings.reader_struggle: A verifier cannot check motivation, benchmark, or corroboration claims.
findings.likely_consequence: Most supporting evidence must be taken on trust.
findings.revision_principle: Every claim that relies on external or visual evidence must point to something the reader can inspect.

location.quote: Figure 1. RWN's error stays near its unshifted level for shifts up to 0.6

findings.observed: Only a caption is provided; the figure, axes, error bars and the s = 0.8 point are absent. No table of per-shift results.
findings.reader_struggle: Readers cannot see the main result the paper relies on.
findings.likely_consequence: The central evidence is reduced to the caption's assertion.
findings.revision_principle: Present the key result visually or tabularly with uncertainty, and let the caption describe what is shown rather than substitute for it.

location.quote: Freezing the statistics recovers about two thirds of the gain.

findings.observed: Headline claims (11-29%, two thirds, no benefit at 0.8) have no numbers, uncertainty or tests shown; intro claims of prevalence and prior-work sufficiency lack presented evidence.
findings.reader_struggle: Verifier cannot match claims to data.
findings.likely_consequence: Claims may be accepted or rejected wholesale rather than evaluated.
findings.revision_principle: Pair each quantitative claim with the data and variability that supports it.

location.quote: Normalization with training statistics is used in essentially all forecasting systems

findings.observed: Several overstrong generalizations in the introduction and a capacity-vs-statistics attribution in the discussion that the design does not test.
findings.reader_struggle: Experts notice claims going beyond the evidence.
findings.likely_consequence: Credibility of the careful parts of the paper is reduced.
findings.revision_principle: Match the strength of every statement to the evidence actually presented.

findings.observed: The paper is short; the abstract result restatement is the only repetition and it is not harmful.
findings.reader_struggle: Works: no wasted reading.
findings.likely_consequence: No harm.
findings.revision_principle: Keep repetition limited to deliberate summary.

location.quote: RWN-fixed freezes them after the first 48 post-shift steps

findings.observed: Three variants are introduced in one dense paragraph; otherwise the load is low because the paper is brief.
findings.reader_struggle: Minor friction keeping RWN vs RWN-fixed straight and understanding what 'freezes' implies.
findings.likely_consequence: Some readers misread the ablation direction.
findings.revision_principle: Introduce each compared condition with its purpose, not only its definition.

findings.observed: Explicit RQs and contribution list orient the reader; sections map to them.
findings.reader_struggle: Minor: no pointer from RQ2 to where the ablation result is reported.
findings.likely_consequence: Readers find their way easily.
findings.revision_principle: Tie each result back to the question it answers.

location.quote: the results suggest that stale statistics, rather than capacity, account for much of the error here

findings.observed: The takeaway is stated but not connected to practice (e.g., when to use RWN, what the 0.8 boundary means for deployment).
findings.reader_struggle: A robustness researcher is left to infer the practical implication.
findings.likely_consequence: The finding is remembered as a narrow synthetic result without actionable meaning.
findings.revision_principle: State the implication for the reader's own work within the tested scope.

inference_issues.missing_link: Superlative prevalence claim with no presented evidence; reference omitted.

inference_issues.claim_text: Normalization with training statistics is used in essentially all forecasting systems [R2, R3, R4, R5, R6].
inference_issues.missing_link: No survey or evidence of universality; citations untraceable.

inference_issues.claim_text: Prior work has shown that per-window normalization fixes distribution shift in general [R2].
inference_issues.missing_link: 'Fixes ... in general' is unsupported and contradicts the paper's own finding of no clear benefit at s = 0.8 and its level-shift-only scope.

inference_issues.claim_text: the results suggest that stale statistics, rather than capacity, account for much of the error here
inference_issues.missing_link: Capacity was held fixed, not varied, so its relative contribution cannot be assessed.

inference_issues.claim_text: Under shift, RWN reduced MAE by 11–29% across s = 0.2–0.6 (Figure 1)
inference_issues.missing_link: No per-shift MAE, no seed variability or test under shift, no numbers for s = 0.8; figure not included.

inference_issues.claim_text: Freezing the statistics recovers about two thirds of the gain.
inference_issues.missing_link: No ablation numbers, shift level(s) or variability reported; RWN-fixed uses oracle knowledge of shift onset.
Corroboration asserted with no description of [R5]'s findings and no reference list.

inference_issues.claim_text: Introduction frames the question in terms of deployed forecasters and all forecasting systems.
inference_issues.missing_link: Discussion limits the evidence to one synthetic series, fixed capacity, level shifts only; the introduction's framing is not bounded accordingly.

objective_discrepancies: Objective asks how much gain depends on continued adaptation; the paper gives 'about a third' but no numbers, shift level or uncertainty, so the reader cannot judge that answer.

Objective says the reader should learn where the finding stops; the paper states no clear benefit at s = 0.8 but gives no data for it, and its introduction claims prior work already fixes distribution shift in general, blurring the boundary.
The paper presents a 'capacity-controlled comparison' as a contribution and draws a statistics-vs-capacity conclusion, which goes beyond the objective and beyond what fixed capacity can show.
